name: Autonomous Computer-Use & Browser Agent Architecture
tagline: Never execute unverified DOM/web-page instructions directly—isolate every browser session in a Firecracker microVM and gate irreversible actions behind human confirmation.
purpose: Computer-Use and Browser Agents pair a Vision-Language Planner (observing screenshots + DOM Accessibility Trees) with an isolated microVM sandbox, prompt-injection guardrails, and human-in-the-loop gates.

spark.summary: Computer-Use and Browser Agents pair a Vision-Language Planner (observing screenshots + DOM Accessibility Trees) with an isolated microVM sandbox, prompt-injection guardrails, and human-in-the-loop gates.
spark.keyTakeaway: When batching and tail latency compete for accelerator cycles, never execute unverified DOM/web-page instructions directly—isolate every browser session in a Firecracker microVM and gate irreversible actions behind human confirmation.
spark.byteSummary:
Autonomous browser and computer-use agents navigate arbitrary web UIs by running an iterative observe-plan-act loop: capturing the viewport screenshot and compressed DOM Accessibility Tree, predicting a grounded `(action, x, y, text)` step, and executing it inside Chromium.

Running headless browsers directly on host containers exposes internal cloud metadata endpoints (`169.254.169.254`) and host filesystems to SSRF and indirect prompt injection hidden inside web pages. Production architectures isolate every session inside a **Firecracker microVM** (< 125 ms snapshot boot) with an egress proxy allowlist and separate untrusted page DOM content from system instructions.

To prevent runaway loops and irreversible mistakes (wire transfers, deletions), steps checkpoint durably via Temporal/state logs and pause at a **Human-in-the-Loop Confirmation Gate** for high-risk actions.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Autonomous Computer-Use & Browser Agent Architecture without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When batching and tail latency compete for accelerator cycles, never execute unverified DOM/web-page instructions directly—isolate every browser session in a Firecracker microVM and gate irreversible actions behind human confirmation.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When Autonomous Computer-Use & Browser Agent Architecture experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

cards.label: Zero Cross-Tenant Reuse
cards.detail: Destroy each microVM after task completion so cookies and DOM storage never leak.

cards.label: Metadata Shield
cards.detail: Drop all packets to 169.254.169.254, 10.0.0.0/8, and localhost at the host TAP interface.
